html:
Keti Koti, Sranan for "the chains are broken", is the celebration of 1 July 1863, when the Netherlands abolished slavery in Suriname and its Caribbean islands.

The Dutch were among the last in the Caribbean to end slavery, decades after Britain's Slavery Abolition Act of 1833. Owners were paid compensation for each slave; the enslaved got nothing. Freed people were made to work ten more years on the plantations under state supervision, until 1873.

Many then left for Paramaribo, and the planters turned to contract workers from Asia, the Indians and the Javanese. Keti Koti is a public holiday in Suriname, and in 2023 the Dutch king apologised for slavery during its celebration.
sum: Keti Koti, Sranan for "the chains are broken", is the celebration of 1 July 1863, when the Netherlands abolished slavery in Suriname and its Caribbean islands.
